Every session ends with questions, and some of them are tough. Here is the method I teach. It has three steps. First, say what you cannot answer. Do not hide it. I cannot give you the exact figure today. Second, say what you can answer, right away. What I can tell you is that the number went down for three quarters. Third, offer to get back to the person, with a day. I will send you the figure on Thursday. People in the room do not expect you to know everything. They expect you to be honest about what you know. If you do these three things, a tough question will make you look more serious, not less.

In my second week, a classmate pushed back on my case. He asked for our default rate in one sector, and I could not remember it. Ten years ago I would apologize for a full minute. This time I said, fair point, I cannot give you the exact figure off the top of my head, but I can tell you it is under two percent, and I will get back to you tonight. He nodded and the session moved on. That night I sent him the number in two lines. The next morning he sat next to me at breakfast. He said he liked that I admitted it. I was not able to answer the question, but I was able to answer the person.
